title: Encrypted DNS Provisioning RFC 9464 Client Policy Architecture
purpose: Define the pure client-side policy boundary for consuming RFC 9464 ENCDNS_IP* and ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO provisioning results.
design_summary: The client-policy slice consumes already-decoded CFG_REPLY or CFG_SET ENCDNS_IP* attributes and optional ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO data, prefers encrypted resolvers over classic INTERNAL_IP*_DNS addresses, expands conveyed resolver addresses into session targets sorted by service priority, routes split-tunnel INTERNAL_DNS_DOMAIN names to encrypted resolvers, rejects non-preconfigured NULL-authenticated responder data, and models certificate validation as ADN validation or SHA2-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo digest validation with non-recoverable failure on mismatch.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is immutable and side-effect free. It does not open DNS sessions, modify OS resolver state, parse IKEv2 messages, or own IPsec connection state.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Malformed ENCDNS_IP* attributes are rejected during decode before policy use.
Encrypted resolver endpoints are produced only from CFG_REPLY or CFG_SET attributes.
NULL-authenticated responder data is ignored unless the initiator is explicitly preconfigured to accept it.
ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO with SHA2-256 must match the resolver certificate SubjectPublicKeyInfo digest when it applies to the endpoint ADN.
Digest or ADN validation failure is represented as a non-recoverable resolver-certificate failure.
risks: This slice does not implement full IKEv2 Configuration Payload exchange processing.
This slice does not install resolvers into the host operating system.
This slice relies on callers to supply the TLS certificate ADN-match signal or SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes from their TLS stack.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The policy boundary keeps RFC 9464 resolver selection and validation decisions testable without coupling Incursa.Quic.Dns to a specific IPsec/IKEv2 implementation or platform resolver API.
